newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares fail to hit new record high.
newsitem.headline: German shares fail to hit new record high.

text.p: German shares, bolstered by overnight Wall Street gains and a firmer dollar, were higher in early bourse dealings on Wednesday but failed to find enough strength to reach a new record high.
The 30-share DAX index was up 26.51 points at 4,408.20 points. The blue-chip index reached a daily high so far at 4,417.71 points but failed to reach the all-time high at 4,418.64 points.
"The fundamentals right now are actually very good to keep on posting gains but the buy orders are lacking at the moment," said one Frankfurt dealer.
The IBIS DAX has gained about 50 points so far this week from last Friday's closing level of 4,368 points but traders said profit-taking on recent advances has capped gains.
"We keep trying to move higher but profit-taking keeps setting us back," said one dealer.
The market continued to focus on banks amid ongoing speculation for more mergers after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank announced last week their plans to merge.
BHF-Bank AG said on Wednesday it expected to post a satisfactory overall profit for 1997 after group pre-tax profit rose 10.4 percent to 181 million marks in the first six months.
Shares in BHF, considered a top takeover target, were down one mark at 58.50 marks even though some dealers said the results were generally in line with market expectations.
Other banking shares were mostly higher. Deutsche Bank AG rose 2.70 marks to 122.40 marks and Commerzbank AG rose 25 pfennigs to 62 marks but Dresdner Bank AG fell 40 pfennigs to 84.80 marks.
Hypo-Bank was up 1.20 marks at 77.00 marks, while Vereinsbank advanced four marks to 102.50 marks.
"The whole sector is up on speculation for more deals," said one trader. "It's a key factor driving the DAX higher."

Among other shares, carmaker Volkswagen AG was up 18.50 marks at 1,374.50 marks after saying in recent days that it was adding extra shifts at some VW and Audi factories due to high demand for models.
Puma AG was down 1.70 marks at 51.10 marks on further selling tied to speculation abating that the sportswear group was a takeover target.
